page.title: CodeVetter — Execution-backed verification for coding agents
page.description: Bind the requested task to the exact change, run repository-owned checks, and keep a pass, fail, or unverified verdict with its evidence.

hero.title: AI writes code fast. It leaves it *unverified.*
hero.lede: CodeVetter binds the requested task to the exact change, runs your repository's own checks, and keeps a pass, fail, or unverified verdict with the evidence and limits behind it.
hero.note: Apple silicon · open source (ISC) · no CodeVetter account

blocks.title: The unit of trust is *the whole chain.*
blocks.lede: A finding or a green command alone is not proof. CodeVetter keeps task identity, execution, evidence, and uncertainty connected, so another engineer, or another agent, can re-check the result.

points.title: Task and change, bound
points.body: The requested outcome and the exact agent revision travel together, so the verifier cannot quietly grade an easier task.

points.title: Checks decide
points.body: Repository-owned tests, builds, browser flows and API checks set the verdict boundary. A model can suggest what to test; execution decides.

points.title: Unknown stays unknown
points.body: Missing or irrelevant evidence produces unverified, not a confidence score dressed up as success.

items.title: Point at the line *the verdict is about.*
items.body: A failing check is linked back to the exact change that caused it, with the command, the bounded output and the limitation, so a reviewer can confirm it in seconds instead of re-running everything.

detail.alt: CodeVetter review workbench: line 12 of portfolio.tsx, if (total >= 0), is flagged as the line the unverified finding is about

items.title: Run the exact change from *your repository.*
items.body: The Apple-silicon release bundles the codevetter CLI and a local MCP sidecar inside the app. Provider-backed review needs a supported local agent CLI; repository-owned checks remain the verdict boundary.

code.label: zsh — ~/work/auth-service
code.code:
# bundled at /Applications/CodeVetter.app/Contents/MacOS/codevetter
$ codevetter check     --range main...HEAD     --task "Reject expired sessions"     --json

✗ fail        pnpm test auth/session.test.ts
✓ pass        pnpm typecheck
? unverified  browser refresh journey

blocks.title: Proof that survives *the next question.*
blocks.lede: The public corpus measures a narrow recognition task. It is not evidence of production-wide accuracy or adoption, and the page says so.

blocks.title: Models can suggest. *Execution decides.*
blocks.lede: No placeholder plans, unsupported installers, or hosted-service promises. Optional model review goes straight to the provider you configure.

points.title: macOS · Apple silicon
points.body: The current GitHub release publishes an aarch64 DMG and updater archive. Other platforms are not published yet.

points.title: Local, no account
points.body: Product state and verification evidence live on your machine. Model review uses the Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter credentials you configure.

points.title: Open source · ISC
points.body: The repository, benchmark cases, scorer, docs, and release workflows are public on GitHub.

blocks.title: Understand *the boundary.*
blocks.lede: Scope, evidence, and availability, answered plainly.

items.a: An execution-backed verification and evaluation system for coding agents. It connects a requested task and exact agent change to executable checks, retained evidence, explicit limitations, and a pass, fail, or unverified verdict.

items.q: Is it another AI code reviewer?
items.a: Review is one input, not the authority. A model can identify suspicious code and suggest what to test, but CodeVetter treats task-relevant execution evidence as the verdict boundary.

items.q: Does my repository go to a CodeVetter server?
items.a: No hosted verification backend is required. Product state and execution evidence stay local. If you start an optional provider-backed review, selected prompt and code context go directly to the provider you configured.
Local checks, stored evidence, and the desktop viewer work without a CodeVetter service. Reviews that call Anthropic, OpenAI, or OpenRouter still need network access to that provider.
Only the declared task and evidence boundary. A pass does not prove behavior that was never checked, and missing or irrelevant evidence stays unverified instead of becoming confidence.
The current GitHub release has an Apple-silicon macOS DMG and updater archive. Source is ISC-licensed. Other platform installers and a Homebrew cask are not published yet.

blocks.title: “Looks good” is *not a verdict.*
blocks.lede: Inspect the evidence contract first, then download the current local desktop build from the GitHub release.
blocks.note: No CodeVetter account · local SQLite state · ISC license

footer.summary: Execution-backed verification for coding-agent changes. Preserve the task, exact change, executable evidence, limitations, and a measurable verdict.
